terms.comment: Morgan–Owens’s phrase, “Italian squash”, for this variety of Cucurbita pepo. Classically cucurbita is a gourd (Col. 11.3.48; Plin. NH 19.69, Lewis & Short); modern Latin carried the name over to the squashes, which come from the New World (M-O s.v. squash: gourd).

Our diminutive of cucurbita for the small squash. Its attested senses are a wild gourd (Scrib. Comp. 106) and the physician’s cupping-glass (Cels. 2.11; 3.18) (Lewis & Short), so the vegetable sense is our extension.

sources: Theodōrus et pater: Epp. VI–VII and Culīna Theodōrī.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.vv. squash: zucchini, courgette; squash: gourd.
